source.export_note: Extracted from the ProCARE appendix benchmark task tables.

prompt_levels.name: Goal
prompt_levels.description: Study objective only; system may find feasible variables and disclose limitations.

prompt_levels.name: Goal+Approach
prompt_levels.description: Study objective plus approach-level methodological guidance.

prompt_levels.name: Goal+Method
prompt_levels.description: Study objective plus specific table, field, anchor, or method constraints.

core_questions.question: Characterize the analyzable HCC cohort, including enrollment, baseline characteristics, and clinical staging.
Assess longitudinal follow-up completeness and data density.
Assess data readiness for downstream endpoint analyses.
Summarize AE/SAE screening rates and the availability of detailed event records.
Describe postoperative laboratory safety signals from liver function, hematology, and coagulation panels.
Compare safety proxy signals after major treatment exposures.
Analyze recurrence and recurrence-free survival proxies after surgery.
Analyze overall survival proxies and their relationship to treatment exposure.
Analyze response assessment and longitudinal tumor-marker changes.
Describe postoperative treatment resource utilization and treatment intensity.
Estimate follow-up and testing burden as a resource-use proxy.
Use SF-12 availability and treatment intensity to assess QoL/resource-use feasibility.

instances.core_question: Characterize the analyzable HCC cohort, including enrollment, baseline characteristics, and clinical staging.
instances.prompt_text: Characterize the baseline hepatocellular carcinoma cohort available in the workbook. Deliver a cohort summary suitable for a real-world study report.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Discover `DM`, `SG`, `BCLC`, `CP`, `ECOG`, and subject identifiers.

instances.core_question: Characterize the analyzable HCC cohort, including enrollment, baseline characteristics, and clinical staging.
instances.prompt_text: Characterize the baseline HCC cohort. Build a STROBE-style cohort table covering demographics, surgery, liver function, tumor stage, and performance status.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Use patient-level baseline records, report missingness, and avoid duplicate subject counting.

instances.core_question: Characterize the analyzable HCC cohort, including enrollment, baseline characteristics, and clinical staging.
instances.prompt_text: Produce a baseline cohort table for subjects with valid `Subject_Id`. Join `DM`, `SG`, `BCLC`, `CP`, and baseline `ECOG`; summarize `AGE`, `SEX`, `HEIGHT`, `WEIGHT`, `SGDAT`, `SGTYP`, `BCLC`, `CPRES`, `CPGRA`, and `ECOG`.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Use one baseline row per subject; report variable-level missingness; do not impute incomplete `AGE`.

instances.core_question: Assess longitudinal follow-up completeness and data density.
instances.prompt_text: Assess whether the dataset has sufficient longitudinal follow-up for real-world evidence generation.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Identify visit-level forms and repeated measurements.

instances.core_question: Assess longitudinal follow-up completeness and data density.
instances.prompt_text: Assess longitudinal follow-up completeness across follow-up forms, laboratory panels, tumor-marker tests, ECOG assessments, and efficacy follow-up records.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Use `CPH_FT`, `VT`, laboratory sheets, and `ECOG`; produce visit-level summaries.

instances.core_question: Assess longitudinal follow-up completeness and data density.
instances.prompt_text: Quantify longitudinal data completeness using `CPH_FT`, `VT`, `LB_AFP`, `LB_BB`, `LB_BR`, and `ECOG`; count distinct visits by `Subject_Id`, tabulate availability by `Visit_No`, and estimate follow-up duration from `SG.SGDAT` to the latest `VT.VTDAT1` or `VT.VTDAT2`.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Use `Subject_Id` and `Visit_No`; report subjects with no valid follow-up date.

instances.core_question: Assess data readiness for downstream endpoint analyses.
instances.prompt_text: Evaluate whether the cohort is fit for downstream RWS endpoint analyses.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Reason about exposure, outcome, confounder, and time-anchor variables.

instances.core_question: Assess data readiness for downstream endpoint analyses.
instances.prompt_text: Evaluate endpoint-analysis readiness through a feasibility matrix covering identifiers, surgery date, treatment exposure, recurrence/death endpoints, and baseline confounders.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Include data limitations, not only descriptive counts.

instances.core_question: Assess data readiness for downstream endpoint analyses.
instances.prompt_text: Build a data-readiness matrix by checking `Subject_Id`, `SG.SGDAT`, recurrence dates `VT.PADHDAT`/`VT.PADRDAT`, death dates `VT.DEDAT1`/`VT.DEDAT2`, treatments from `TACE`, `TART`, `IMU`, `PATE`, and confounders `DM.SEX`, `DM.AGE`, `BCLC.BCLC`, `CP.CPGRA`, `ECOG.ECOG`.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Flag sparse or unavailable fields, especially `VT.DEDAT2`; do not invent endpoint fields.

instances.core_question: Summarize AE/SAE screening rates and the availability of detailed event records.
instances.prompt_text: Analyze the adverse-event and serious-adverse-event safety profile in the cohort.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Discover that AE/SAE screening pages exist but detailed event tables are empty in the current workbook.

instances.core_question: Summarize AE/SAE screening rates and the availability of detailed event records.
instances.prompt_text: Analyze AE and SAE safety reporting. Start with screening pages, then check whether detailed AE/SAE records are available for term, onset date, severity, causality, outcome, and seriousness.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Document infeasibility of detailed AE/SAE term analysis when detail tables have no valid records.

instances.core_question: Summarize AE/SAE screening rates and the availability of detailed event records.
instances.prompt_text: Summarize AE/SAE reporting completeness using `AE_HQ.AEYN` and `SAE_HQ.SAEYN`; inspect `AE.AETERM`, `AE.AESTDAT`, `AE.AESEV`, `AE.AEREL`, `AE.AESAE`, `SAE.SAESTDAT`, and `SAE.SAESEV`.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Compute screening prevalence by subject; terminate detail-level analysis if `AE` and `SAE` contain zero valid records.

instances.core_question: Describe postoperative laboratory safety signals from liver function, hematology, and coagulation panels.
instances.prompt_text: Identify laboratory safety signals after surgery.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Use longitudinal laboratory sheets rather than relying only on AE tables.

instances.core_question: Describe postoperative laboratory safety signals from liver function, hematology, and coagulation panels.
instances.prompt_text: Identify post-surgical laboratory safety signals by summarizing liver function, hematology, and coagulation markers over follow-up visits.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Use lab value/result-judgment pairs and visit dates; report abnormal-result flags when available.

instances.core_question: Describe postoperative laboratory safety signals from liver function, hematology, and coagulation panels.
instances.prompt_text: Generate a post-surgical laboratory safety profile anchored at `SG.SGDAT`; use `LB_BB.LBBBDAT`, `ALTRES`, `ASTRES`, `TBILRES`, `ALBRES`; `LB_BR.BRDAT`, `WBCRES`, `HBRES`, `PLTRES`; and `LB_TT.LBTTDAT`, `PTRES`, `INRRES`, `DDIMRES`.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Summarize baseline and postoperative windows; use available-case denominators and `_SIG` flags when numeric thresholds are unavailable.

instances.core_question: Compare safety proxy signals after major treatment exposures.
instances.prompt_text: Compare safety patterns across major postoperative treatment exposures.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Identify TACE, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and retreatment exposure sheets.

instances.core_question: Compare safety proxy signals after major treatment exposures.
instances.prompt_text: Compare safety proxy signals by treatment exposure using TACE, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and postoperative retreatment groups.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Compare AE/SAE screening and laboratory abnormalities descriptively; avoid causal claims.

instances.core_question: Compare safety proxy signals after major treatment exposures.
instances.prompt_text: Compare treatment-associated safety proxies using exposure indicators from `TACE.TACEDAT`, `TART.TARSDAT`, `IMU.IMUSDAT`, and `PATE.PATEYN`; calculate screening rates from `AE_HQ.AEYN` and `SAE_HQ.SAEYN`; summarize post-exposure laboratory signals from `LB_BB`, `LB_BR`, and `LB_TT`.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Report confounder imbalance using `BCLC.BCLC`, `CP.CPGRA`, and `ECOG.ECOG`; frame results as descriptive safety proxies.

instances.core_question: Analyze recurrence and recurrence-free survival proxies after surgery.
instances.prompt_text: Analyze recurrence-related outcomes after surgery.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Locate surgery dates and recurrence dates in `VT`.

instances.core_question: Analyze recurrence and recurrence-free survival proxies after surgery.
instances.prompt_text: Analyze recurrence-free outcomes using surgery date as time origin, recurrence events from follow-up records, and clinically relevant baseline risk strata.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Handle multiple follow-up visits and competing or missing dates.

instances.core_question: Analyze recurrence and recurrence-free survival proxies after surgery.
instances.prompt_text: Estimate recurrence-free survival proxies using `SG.SGDAT` as index date; define recurrence as the earliest non-missing `VT.PADHDAT` or `VT.PADRDAT`; censor at latest `VT.VTDAT1` or `VT.VTDAT2`; stratify by `BCLC.BCLC`, `CP.CPGRA`, and exposure from `TACE`, `TART`, `IMU`, or `PATE`.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Use earliest valid recurrence date and valid time ordering; generate Kaplan-Meier curves only when dates are sufficient.

instances.core_question: Analyze overall survival proxies and their relationship to treatment exposure.
instances.prompt_text: Analyze overall survival patterns in the cohort.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Identify death dates and follow-up dates.

instances.core_question: Analyze overall survival proxies and their relationship to treatment exposure.
instances.prompt_text: Analyze overall survival by deriving time from surgery to death or last follow-up and comparing clinically meaningful strata.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Use `DEDAT1`/`DEDAT2` and `VT` follow-up dates; disclose death-date limitations.

instances.core_question: Analyze overall survival proxies and their relationship to treatment exposure.
instances.prompt_text: Estimate overall-survival proxies using `SG.SGDAT` as index date; define death date as earliest non-missing `VT.DEDAT1` or `VT.DEDAT2`; censor at latest valid `VT.VTDAT1` or `VT.VTDAT2`; compare treatment exposures and adjust or stratify descriptively by `DM.SEX`, `DM.AGE`, `BCLC.BCLC`, `CP.CPGRA`, and `ECOG.ECOG` when available.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Note that `DEDAT2` is unavailable in the current data; avoid over-adjusted models when events are limited.

instances.core_question: Analyze response assessment and longitudinal tumor-marker changes.
instances.prompt_text: Evaluate treatment response and tumor-marker dynamics over follow-up.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Combine efficacy assessment and biomarker sheets.

instances.core_question: Analyze response assessment and longitudinal tumor-marker changes.
instances.prompt_text: Evaluate response and tumor-marker dynamics by summarizing hospital/telephone efficacy evaluations and longitudinal AFP, CA199, and DCP trajectories by visit and exposure.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Combine categorical response information with biomarker trends.

instances.core_question: Analyze response assessment and longitudinal tumor-marker changes.
instances.prompt_text: Analyze response and tumor-marker trends using `VT.CEVYN`, `VT.CUEV`, `VT.VTDAT1`, `VT.VTDAT2`, plus `LB_AFP.LBAFPDAT`, `AFPRES`, `CA199RES`, and `DCPRES`; align measurements by `Subject_Id` and date relative to `SG.SGDAT`; summarize trajectories by exposure to `TACE`, `TART`, or `IMU`.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: If formal response criteria are not encoded, report observed categories and marker changes without RECIST claims.

instances.core_question: Describe postoperative treatment resource utilization and treatment intensity.
instances.prompt_text: Analyze postoperative treatment resource utilization in the cohort.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Recognize that the task concerns utilization rather than direct cost.

instances.core_question: Describe postoperative treatment resource utilization and treatment intensity.
instances.prompt_text: Analyze postoperative treatment resource utilization by quantifying use and timing of TACE, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, postoperative retreatment, and concomitant medications.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Use procedure and drug counts with dates as utilization proxies.

instances.core_question: Describe postoperative treatment resource utilization and treatment intensity.
instances.prompt_text: Quantify treatment-utilization intensity by deriving per-subject counts and time-to-first-use for `TACE.TACEDAT`, `TART.TARSDAT`, `IMU.IMUSDAT`, `PATE.PATEYN`/`PATETR*`, and `CM.CMCAT`/`CMSTDAT`; summarize utilization distributions and stratify by `BCLC.BCLC` and recurrence status when feasible.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Explicitly state that no direct cost or billing variables are present.

instances.core_question: Estimate follow-up and testing burden as a resource-use proxy.
instances.prompt_text: Estimate follow-up and testing burden associated with the RWS cohort.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Use visit and form/test counts as burden proxies.

instances.core_question: Estimate follow-up and testing burden as a resource-use proxy.
instances.prompt_text: Estimate follow-up and testing burden by counting follow-up visits, efficacy assessments, laboratory panels, tumor-marker checks, coagulation tests, ECOG assessments, and QoL forms per patient.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Summarize burden by patient and visit.

instances.core_question: Estimate follow-up and testing burden as a resource-use proxy.
instances.prompt_text: Build a follow-up resource-burden profile by counting records in `CPH_FT`, `VT`, `LB_AFP`, `LB_BB`, `LB_BR`, `LB_TT`, `ECOG`, and `SF`; compute total follow-up forms/tests, median counts per subject, and distribution by `Visit_No`; use `SG.SGDAT` and latest `VT.VTDAT1`/`VT.VTDAT2` to contextualize burden over time.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Frame the result as utilization burden, not economic cost.

instances.core_question: Use SF-12 availability and treatment intensity to assess QoL/resource-use feasibility.
instances.prompt_text: Explore quality-of-life evidence and its relationship to treatment burden.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Discover SF-12 sparsity and avoid overclaiming.

instances.core_question: Use SF-12 availability and treatment intensity to assess QoL/resource-use feasibility.
instances.prompt_text: Explore QoL and treatment burden using SF-12 items when available; summarize missingness and compare available QoL responses across treatment-utilization groups.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Emphasize sparse SF item completeness.

instances.core_question: Use SF-12 availability and treatment intensity to assess QoL/resource-use feasibility.
instances.prompt_text: Analyze QoL/resource-use proxy feasibility by inspecting `SF.SFYN` and `SF1`--`SF12`; compute complete-item availability; when enough records exist, summarize item-level or total scores by exposure groups from `TACE`, `TART`, `IMU`, and `PATE`; otherwise report feasibility and missingness only.
instances.required_or_expected_evidence: Terminate formal QoL comparison when usable SF-12 item records are too sparse.
